jesus.o: Adoptive father: Jesus was conceived by the Holy Spirit (Matthew 1:20); he was the son of Joseph "as was supposed" (Luke 3:23).

zorobabel.o: 1 Chronicles 3:19 names Pedaiah as the father of Zerubbabel; Ezra, Haggai, and Matthew say he was the son of Shealtiel.

arbres.desc: The ten generations from Adam to Noah, and the line of Cain.
The table of nations (main lineages) and the descendants of Shem down to Terah.
Terah and his sons: Abraham, Nahor, and Haran—from whom came Isaac, Rebekah, Leah, Rachel, Lot and his sons.
The twelve sons of Jacob and their mother, in order of birth, along with Dinah and Joseph's sons.
The priestly tribe: from Levi to Moses, Aaron, Miriam, and their sons.
The royal line: Judah, Perez, Boaz and Ruth, Jesse and his children.
The wives and sons of David: Amnon, Absalom, Adonijah, Solomon, Nathan…
From Solomon to Zedekiah, then Zerubbabel: the dynasty of David, father to son.
Omri, Ahab and Jezebel, and their daughter Athaliah who reigned over Judah.
Four generations on the throne of Israel, as God had promised Jehu.
Israel's first king, his children, and his grandson Mephibosheth.
Joseph and Mary, Jesus and his brothers and sisters named in the Gospels.
arbres.note: Protestants read these brothers and sisters as children of Mary and Joseph born after Jesus; other traditions see them as cousins or half-brothers.

arbres.desc: Herod the Great and his descendants, from the massacre in Bethlehem to Paul's trial.
arbres.note: The Bible names these kings without always specifying their kinship; missing links come from the Jewish historian Flavius Josephus (first century).

arbres.desc: From Abraham to Jesus, through Solomon and the kings of Judah: Matthew shows in Jesus the heir of the promises made to Abraham and David.
arbres.note: Matthew groups the list in three sets of fourteen generations (Matthew 1:17) and skips some kings: "beget" can mean "be the ancestor of." He also names four women before Mary—Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, and "the wife of Uriah"—some of whom were foreign.

arbres.desc: From Jesus back to Adam, "son of God": Luke traces all of human history to show in Jesus the Savior of all.
arbres.note: After David, Luke goes through Nathan rather than Solomon. This is often explained as follows: Luke would follow Mary's line, or Joseph had a legal father and a natural father. Some names have no certain equivalent in the Old Testament (Cainan, for example, comes from the Greek version of Genesis).
